message.content: Dense inference activates all parameters per token, maximizing compute and memory bandwidth use but with no routing overhead. Sparse expert routing activates only selected experts, reducing compute and memory bandwidth per token, but adds routing overhead from the gating step. Dense inference avoids load balancing issues since all experts are always used; sparse routing risks imbalance where some experts are overloaded and others underused, hurting utilization. Overall, dense inference is simpler and uniformly utilized, while sparse routing saves compute/bandwidth at the cost of routing logic and potential load imbalance.
